video_title: Denver Nuggets Training Camp Day Three | Practice Media Availability

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Christian Braun's improvement in ball-handling and utility
quotes.excerpt: I thought he improved last year too. In big moments when there's better defenders, everybody's going to struggle.
quotes.quote: I thought he improved last year too. In big moments when there's better defenders, everybody's going to struggle. Last year, I gave him the ball a lot after timeouts to initiate, especially Jamal off the ball, specifically to get Jamal the ball in the wing or wherever we want to get him a tight spot like the elbow. You just got to keep working at it. Just because these guys are pros doesn't mean they can't get better at stuff.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman says Christian Braun is continuing to improve his ball-handling and playmaking, noting that even pros have to keep working at it to handle pressure in big moments.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Over-teaching dribbling skills in the US basketball system
quotes.excerpt: We over-teach in the US all this dribble, all this crap that we do. Straight lines are okay.
quotes.quote: We over-teach in the US all this dribble, all this crap that we do. Straight lines are okay, and getting to a spot is okay. A lot of people make a lot of money off doing things that should be tricks at a party as opposed to just getting to a location on the court to be successful.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman is critical of how basketball is taught in the US, saying we over-teach dribbling tricks instead of focusing on getting to a spot to be successful.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Christian Braun's physical health and explosive movement
quotes.excerpt: When something that is God-given to you that has helped you be a professional basketball player is taken
quotes.quote: When something that is God-given to you that has helped you be a professional basketball player is taken away from you, it's a big deal. And when you run in transition, you're not dunking the ball, you're laying the ball up with athletes that are trailing you, it changes things. So I think getting that back is key.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman emphasizes the importance of Christian Braun regaining his explosive movement, noting that when a player loses the physical gifts that made them a pro, it changes everything.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Nemhard's impact on pick-and-roll defense
quotes.excerpt: He embarrassed our pick-and-roll defense last year. I did not rewatch that tape.
quotes.quote: He embarrassed our pick-and-roll defense last year. I did not rewatch that tape. But he has a special gift. He's a speed-burst kind of guy, his feet hit the paint. Today he made three or four really nice plays just in the pick-and-roll.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman praised Ryan Nemhard for his pick-and-roll ability, recalling how he embarrassed the Nuggets defense last year and noting he has a special gift for getting into the paint.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: The emergence of a new class of two-way players
quotes.excerpt: The two-way now it's need-based, because there's so much talent out there.
quotes.quote: The two-way now it's need-based, because there's so much talent out there. It's interesting for these guys because they're so close to being on an NBA roster. You look at a guy like Colin in Phoenix, he stayed with it and he got paid, and he's a really good player.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman discusses the evolution of two-way players, noting that the system is now need-based because there is so much talent available.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of crashing the offensive glass
quotes.excerpt: When you create that contact, don't let them get behind you in a sense where you're keeping everything
quotes.quote: When you create that contact, don't let them get behind you in a sense where you're keeping everything in front, which you know, even if the ball handler wasn't touched and he gets a little bit ahead, like he's kind of caught in more of a wash. I've seen this work, and as long as we commit to it, like I think that's a big thing about any scheme you do, you have to commit.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson says the key to the Nuggets' rebounding scheme is commitment, noting that as long as players commit to the principles, the system works.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Decisiveness and free-flowing movement in the offense
quotes.excerpt: It's decisiveness in our actions and our free flow, understanding where Yoke, where Jamal, where AG, where CB
quotes.quote: It's decisiveness in our actions and our free flow, understanding where Yoke, where Jamal, where AG, where CB, where they turn, where they go, and then being able to make a quick decisive play off of that. I think that's where I started to get a little bit better at last year, where I started to produce a little more, and it makes the game a lot simpler too.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson says the Nuggets offense is focused on decisiveness and free-flowing movement, learning how to play off of Jokic, Jamal, AG, and CB to make the game simpler.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Building the foundation for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: It's that rebounding principle, it's that crash principle, it's defensive gap principles, rotation principles.
quotes.quote: It's that rebounding principle, it's that crash principle, it's defensive gap principles, rotation principles. We're putting in some of that baseline stuff, but we're going to build it up over the course of the season to get us ready for those moments. But I'm encouraged by it. I'm encouraged by it. I think we've found areas to grow and we're attacking them.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson says the team is currently focused on building a foundation of defensive gap and rebounding principles that they will continue to develop throughout the season.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Impressions of teammates Alpha, Bryson, and Trayvon
quotes.excerpt: I really like Alpha. You can just see that maturity he has from his professional experience.
quotes.quote: I really like Alpha. You can just see that maturity he has from his professional experience. He's a menace on defense, an absolute menace on defense, very much like accountable in the right space on offense, can knock down shots. I really like what I've seen from him so far. Bryson and Trayvon are really good young players. Trayvon's athleticism, length, he's all over the place, runs the floor, offensive rebound. Same with Bryce, and those guys have been doing really well. Tais has been playing really well too, and so has Marvin. They've all looked pretty good and you can tell that they've been put in a lot of work.
quotes.social_post: Cam Johnson is impressed with the young players in camp, calling Alpha a menace on defense and praising the athleticism and work ethic of Bryson and Trayvon.
